What do V8 and libuv do in Node?
options: V8 runs JS. libuv provides the event loop, timers, and async I/O
libuv runs JS. V8 only draws the console
Both do the same thing: they read files
V8 is npm. libuv is package.json

questions.text: Why is JS in Node called single-threaded?
options: All I/O runs on the same thread as your for-loop
JS runs on one thread. libuv I/O may use a thread pool, but the callback returns to the JS thread
Node starts a thread per require
Single-threaded means you cannot open two files

questions.text: What is an error-first callback in Node?
options: The first argument is the result; the error is on this
Errors are thrown; the callback only carries data
The first argument is Error or null, then the data
The error is the last argument, as in the browser

questions.text: How does fs.readFile differ from fs.readFileSync in an HTTP server?
options: Neither blocks the loop. Only the name differs
readFileSync is faster, so it belongs in every request
readFile yields to the loop and does not hold the JS thread during the read. readFileSync blocks the loop until the read finishes

questions.text: What does require do on a second load of the same file?
options: It returns the cached module.exports and does not run the file again
It always runs the file from scratch
It deletes the file from disk
It works once per process; the second call throws

questions.text: Where does __dirname come from in CommonJS?
options: It is a browser global; Node only proxies it
Node wraps the file in a function and passes that file’s directory path
It is process.cwd(), always the directory where you launched node

questions.text: How do you enable ESM for a package’s .js files in Node?
options: Node cannot do ESM; even .mjs does not work

questions.text: What is process.argv in Node?
options: The argument array: the node path, the script path, then the command-line arguments

questions.text: What type are process.env values?
options: Strings. Even numeric-looking values arrive as strings
Node parses numbers and booleans for you

questions.text: Is EventEmitter e.emit("x") synchronous?
options: No. emit always goes through setTimeout(0)
Yes. Listeners run at once, on the same stack, before emit returns
Only if the event name is data
emit puts listeners on the thread pool

questions.text: Does Node have a global window?
options: Yes. It is an alias of process
Yes, the same as in the browser
No. window is a browser global. Node uses globalThis for the global object

questions.text: What do npm scripts from package.json do?
options: They are comments; npm does not run them
They only run in the browser
Each script starts a separate Node cluster
npm run executes the command and puts node_modules/.bin on PATH

Why does Node need libuv?
questions.answer: The event loop, timers, sockets, and async I/O that JS cannot do alone.

questions.text: What is the first argument of a classic Node callback?
questions.answer: An error, or null when there is no error.

Why is readFileSync dangerous inside a request handler?
questions.answer: It blocks the JS thread and the event loop until the disk answers.

questions.text: What is in process.argv[1]?
questions.answer: The path to the script being run. argv[0] is the node binary.

questions.text: How does EventEmitter.once differ from on?
questions.answer: once removes the listener after the first call.

questions.text: What does a Buffer store?
questions.answer: Raw bytes of a fixed length, not a JS string.

questions.text: What does a second require of the same file return?
questions.answer: The same cached exports, without running the file again.

questions.text: Why is process.exitCode better than a bare process.exit() at the end of work?
questions.answer: The exit code is stored, and the process can finish I/O and then exit on its own.

questions.text: Does ESM have module.exports out of the box?
questions.answer: No. ESM exports with export / export default.

questions.text: What does path.posix.join do with path segments?
questions.answer: It joins them with /, normalizing extra slashes, in POSIX style.
